source_references: Meta/Security/Ops Workstream Track INF Environment Model
freeze_boundary: Draft only. Materializes exactly: the OB-003 rule that liveness must NOT be tied to an external provider, expressed as `const false` so the contract enforces it rather than describing it; the OB-003 rule that readiness reflects the real capability, expressed per capability on MR-004's 'readiness result per capability/scope' and with a module forbidden from reporting itself ready while listing an unready capability; the MR-004 deny-by-default requirement that an unready capability states a reason; the OB-001 and OBS-004 requirement that one correlation identity carries across retry, worker and adapter; the OBS-002 requirement that module and environment appear on every record; and the OB-006 rule that no user content, token or page name becomes a metric label, expressed as a CLOSED label-name set. NOT inferred and open before freeze: the aggregation and probe protocol OB-003 delivers, the alert routing and severity mapping OB-002 delivers, the SLO targets and error-budget arithmetic (OBS-009), the trace propagation wire format (OBS-004), the numeric cardinality budget (see accepted_gaps), and the drain and shutdown states of MR-005, which belong to CTR-MOD-001's lifecycle and are deliberately not duplicated here. Human-readable fields are stable keys, never free text, on the CM-004 and CTR-ERR-001 precedent, because OBS-001 forbids full content on this path and MR-006 requires support to read it without seeing a secret.
untestable_by_fixture: OB-001 requires ONE correlation identity to survive a retry, a worker handoff and an adapter call, and OBS-004 requires the browser, API, outbox, worker and provider spans to join up. Both are properties of a sequence of signals over time, not of any single signal: a fixture can show that a document carries a correlation_id, never that the next document carries the SAME one. OB-003's 'readiness reflects the real capability' is the same shape of claim -- it is agreement between this document and the world, which only a probe against a running module can check. All three need a propagation harness before freeze and are NOT claimed as materialized.
untestable_by_schema: OB-006 requires metric cardinality to be BOUNDED. This schema closes the set of label NAMES, which is what makes `page_name` rejected, but cardinality is a property of the value space and JSON Schema cannot bound how many distinct values a field takes across a population of documents. No numeric budget exists in the baseline and none is invented; the shipped pattern constrains only each value's charset and length. Separately, nothing here checks that `sli_tags.module_key` equals `module.module_key`, or that a `capability_key` in `sli_tags` appears in `readiness.capabilities`, because this validator cannot compare one property's value with another's.

accepted_gaps.examples/accepted-gap-unbounded-error-co: OB-006 requires that metric cardinality is bounded, and this contract does not achieve it. The label NAME set is closed, so user content and page name cannot become dimensions, but nothing bounds the VALUE space of a label that is allowed: this fixture carries an `error_code` label whose value embeds an attempt number and a correlation id, so every failure produces a distinct time series and the metric backend degrades exactly as OB-006 exists to prevent. The contract accepts it because the baseline states the requirement without a numeric budget, and JSON Schema cannot express a population property in any case, so inventing a limit here would be a rule with no source that still would not enforce what OB-006 asks. The A6 observability owner delivering OB-006 and OBS-009 must set the per-label budget and the allowed value vocabulary, and this schema must then constrain each label to it, before freeze.
